complications.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
complications.source_text: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is diagnosed by the persistent elevation of urinary albumin excretion (albuminuria), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m², or other manifestat...

complications.name: Kidney Failure
complications.source_text: CKD can progress to kidney failure requiring dialysis or kidney transplantation and is the leading cause of kidney failure in the U.S. (5).

complications.name: Cardiovascular Disease (CVD)
complications.source_text: In addition, among people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, the presence of CKD markedly increases cardiovascular risk and health care costs (6).

complications.name: Hyperkalemia
complications.source_text: Hyperkalemia resulted in 2.3% discontinuation in the study group compared with 0.9% in the placebo group.

complications.name: Hypokalemia
complications.source_text: Serum potassium should also be monitored in individuals treated with diuretics because these medications can cause hypokalemia, which is associated with cardiovascular risk and mortality (38–40).

complications.name: Diabetic Retinopathy
complications.source_text: It is rare for people with type 1 diabetes to develop kidney disease without retinopathy.

therapeutic_agents.name: ACE inhibitors
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Accordingly, ACE inhibitors and ARBs should not be discontinued for increases in serum creatinine (<30%) in the absence of volume depletion.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: To maximally tolerated dose to prevent the progression of kidney disease and reduce cardiovascular events in those with moderately increased albuminuria (UACR 30–299 mg/g creatinine) or strongly recommended for those with severely increased albuminuria (UACR ≥300 mg/g creatinine) and/or eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2.

therapeutic_agents.name: SGLT2 inhibitors
therapeutic_agents.source_text: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce kidney tubular glucose reabsorption, weight, systemic blood pressure, intraglomerular pressure, and albuminuria and slow GFR loss through mechanisms that appear independent ...
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Recommended for people with type 2 diabetes and CKD with eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m² to reduce CKD progression and cardiovascular events. Can safely continue until kidney failure.

therapeutic_agents.name: Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists
therapeutic_agents.source_text: GLP-1 RAs have also been shown to improve kidney outcomes (104–109).
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Recommended to reduce kidney disease progression and cardiovascular risk in people with type 2 diabetes and CKD.

therapeutic_agents.name: Finerenone
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Finerenone is currently the only nsMRA with proven clinical kidney and cardiovascular benefits.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Recommended to reduce CKD progression and cardiovascular events in people with CKD and albuminuria (if eGFR is ≥25 mL/min/1.73 m²).

therapeutic_agents.name: Metformin
therapeutic_agents.source_text: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) revised its guidance for the use of metformin in CKD in 2016 (114), recommending use of eGFR instead of serum creatinine to guide treatment and expanding...
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Contraindicated in individuals with an eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m². Monitor eGFR while taking metformin. Reassess benefits/risks when eGFR falls to <45 mL/min/1.73 m². Do not initiate if eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73 m². Temporarily discontinue before iodinated contrast imaging procedures in individuals with eGFR 30–60 mL/min/1.73 m².

therapeutic_agents.source_text: Individuals with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² receiving ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) should have serum potassium measured periodically to assess for hyperkalemia.
